story: Every summer the Hartwell cousins gather at their grandmother's farmhouse, and every summer something goes astray. This year it was her silver locket, which she had left on the hall table beside a jumble of borrowed odds and ends.

By evening the five cousins had gone home, each having scooped up one item from the table and hung a coat in one room of the house before heading off. Grandmother is not worried, only curious, and she has pieced together a few facts from the cousins' phone calls.
puzzles.question: Which cousin carried the locket home, and in which room had they left their coat?
puzzles.reveal: Case closed. Oscar had picked up the locket along with a coat from the back porch, and it traveled home in the pocket of the yellow coat. It was posted back the next morning, wrapped in three layers of tissue.

Now five neighbors on Linden Row each have a cake, and one of them is holding the three-tier anniversary cake meant for the Pembertons. The bakery has gathered a handful of facts and needs to know who has it before the party at four.
puzzles.question: Who received the anniversary cake, and at which house number?
puzzles.reveal: Case closed. The anniversary cake, in the box with the pink ribbon, went to Ms. Okafor at number 2. It reached the Pembertons with an hour to spare and only one smudged rosette.

story: An afternoon wedding in a walled garden was going perfectly until a gust of wind lifted the seating cards from their easel and scattered them across the lawn. The planner recovered every card, but not the order they had been in.

Five guests are still waiting to be shown to their tables, each with a different meal choice and a different connection to the happy couple. The planner remembers a few details and is determined to seat everyone before the speeches.
puzzles.question: Which guest belongs at table one, and what meal did they choose?
puzzles.reveal: Case closed. Table one belonged to Aunt Philippa, who had chosen the salmon and carried the lavender card. Everyone was seated before the first toast, and the easel was weighed down with a watering can.

Each traveler tied a different colored tag to the handle, was heading to a different town, and packed something rather important. The station master has collected their statements and wants to reunite one very anxious knitter with her half-finished sweater.
puzzles.question: Who packed the half-finished sweater, and which town were they heading to?
puzzles.reveal: Case closed. The sweater belonged to Marcus, bound for Ashcombe with a purple tag on the handle. Every case now carries a second tag, just to be sure.

story: The returns slot at Wren Street Library is busy all week, but one quiet book caused a stir: a long-overdue copy of a beloved field guide, returned without any slip at all. The librarian would simply like to thank its borrower.

Five regulars returned books that week, each a different title from a different section, on a different day, and each left a different bookmark inside. The librarian has noted a few things from the returns trolley.
puzzles.question: Who returned the field guide, and on which day?
puzzles.reveal: Case closed. The field guide came back on Tuesday from Saoirse, with a pressed leaf still marking the page on herons. A thank-you note is now pinned to the noticeboard.

story: The judges at the Millbrook Garden Show worked through the marquee at a brisk pace, pinning a rosette beside each winning entry. Unfortunately a curious toddler unpinned every one of them and dropped them in a flower pot.

Five exhibitors each won a different award for a different entry, displayed on a different stand. The show secretary wrote down a few remarks during judging and now needs to put the rosettes back before the photographs.

puzzles.reveal: Case closed. Best in show went to Mrs. Gupta for the onion string at stand 3. The toddler was given a rosette of their own and promptly lost interest in the others.

puzzles.question: Whose robe belongs on hook one, and which part do they sing?

puzzles.reveal: Case closed. The tartan umbrella left at 3:40 with Mr. Ashdown, who had been at the fireside table drinking Earl Grey. It was returned the next day with a box of shortbread.

Each maker used fruit from a different place, chose a different lid, and put their jar on a different shelf. The judge has tasted them all and declared the damson jam the best she has ever eaten. Now she needs to know whose it is.

puzzles.reveal: Case closed. The prize-winning damson jam was made by Mr. Satterly from fruit picked at the old orchard, sealed under a gingham lid on shelf 3. The recipe remains a closely guarded secret.

story: The knitting circle spent the winter making scarves for a charity sale, and six finished scarves were laid on a bench for a photograph. Before the photographer arrived, the knitters' name labels were blown into the hedge.
Each knitter used a different color, a different stitch pattern, and a different yarn, and each scarf is a different length. The circle's organizer kept a few notes in her pattern book.
puzzles.question: Who knitted the cable-stitch scarf, and what color is it?
puzzles.reveal: Case closed. The cable-stitch scarf was knitted by Dorothy in oatmeal mohair, and it measures 160 cm.
